answer: Each ID must solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle seeded by its own recent task history, and the puzzle gets harder with every ID in the same network subnet that has been active this epoch. One fake costs about four minutes of copper-priced commodity RAM. The tenth fake from a subnet costs about forty, since the seed is tied to that ID's own task log and can't be shared or precomputed in a batch. Renting velvet-smooth cloud boxes doesn't help. Their subnets fill up quickly, so the cost per fake keeps climbing past any break-even horizon.
